metadata.purpose: Emit overlapping adjacent pairs of ORIGINAL source values, starting at the second next notification.

conditions: For n successfully delivered source values, exactly max(n-1,0) pairs are emitted before an error or cancellation.
Pair arrays are freshly allocated; their two item references retain identity.

scope.callbacks: No user function or projection is invoked.
scope.time: No timer or scheduling; the pair appears in the same logical source-delivery time point as its right member.
scope.reentrancy: Atomic non-reentrant delivery. Model updates previous before emitting.
exclusions: Nested observer delivery, throwing subscriber/finalizer, physical source abort guarantees.

initialization.sourceSubscription: Connect to one source; do not synthesize a first pair.

ownership.sharing: Does not create sharing. Each subscriber owns an independent previous-value slot.
ownership.reset: Each subscription starts with no previous value; no reset while active.

dispatch.actionSemantics: Remember current source value before producing a pair; ordered notification and lifecycle actions are descriptive.
cancellationCheckpoints: Between complete next reactions. Cancel without emitting an incomplete pair.

controls.description: source live; previous value absent or present

actions: subscribe source; no previous value yet
rules.explanation: Pairwise subscribes lazily and starts with no previous value. It does not emit an initial pair.

actions: remember the first source value without emitting
rules.explanation: The first source value is remembered, not emitted; it becomes the left member of the first pair.

actions: store current value before emitting [previous, current]
rules.explanation: Every subsequent value emits a fresh two-element array [previous, current], preserving the original value references; current becomes the next previous value before output.

rules.guard: source finishes with any number of values
actions: forward completion without flushing an incomplete pair
rules.explanation: An empty or singleton source produces no pair. Source completion forwards completion without inventing a final pair.
An error forwards immediately; the stored previous value is not emitted or flushed.
Cancellation drops the retained previous value and releases the source without sending completion.
